info.name: TaskFlow API
info.description:
Tests for the TaskFlow API against the seeded development database (see docs/DATABASE.md).

1. Start PostgreSQL (`docker compose up -d`) and the API (`dotnet run --launch-profile https` in src/TaskFlow.API).
2. Check `baseUrl` in the collection variables (default https://localhost:7103).
3. Run the whole collection in order with the Collection Runner: later requests use tokens and ids saved by earlier ones.

All seeded accounts use the password in the `password` variable. Re-runnable: each run registers and then deletes its own user; folder 5 deletes every task the run created and folder 6 every comment. Those folders also trigger automatic notifications for seeded users (assignments, comments, status changes), which stay as history; folder 7 uses its own throw-away user and removes everything it creates, and so does folder 8.

Responses: success is 200 with `{ isSuccess, data }`; every failure is an RFC 9457 ProblemDetails (`application/problem+json`) with `title` = error type (Validation, Unauthorized, Forbidden, NotFound, Conflict) and `detail` = message. Validation errors from the request validators also carry an `errors` object per field.

Works on tasks it creates, then deletes them and the three tasks from folder 3, so the seed data is unchanged.

7. Notifications
item.description: Automatic notifications and GET /api/notifications, /unread-count, PATCH /{id}/read, POST /read-all. Uses a throw-away user who creates a task that the Manager then assigns, comments, edits and completes, so every notification lands with that user (the actor is never notified, one notification per user per change). At the end the task and the user are deleted, which removes their notifications too. Live delivery over SignalR (/hubs/notifications) is covered by the integration tests; see docs/REALTIME.md.

item.name: Log in as the throw-away user
A new user has no notifications
Throw-away user creates an unassigned task
Manager assigns it to the throw-away user -> TaskAssigned
Manager comments -> CommentAdded (creator and assignee are the same user: one notification)
Throw-away user comments on their own task -> nobody is notified
Manager marks it Done -> TaskCompleted (not also TaskUpdated)
List: newest first, one per change

8. Dashboard
item.description: GET /api/dashboard for the caller. `tasks`, `overdueTasks` and `dueSoonTasks` (next 7 days, not Done) cover every task; `myAssignedTasks`, `myOpenCreatedTasks`, `unreadNotifications` and `recentTasks` (5 most recently updated tasks the caller created or is assigned to) are personal. A throw-away user creates two tasks and checks the exact changes; nobody else is notified, and the tasks and the user are deleted at the end.
